newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher on foreign ownership rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher on foreign ownership rise.

text.p: Anticipation of an inflow of foreign funds on Friday's expansion of the foreign stock ownership ceiling boosted Seoul stocks, brokers said.
They said Jinro Group shares remained strong on an expected announcement of an aid package.
The composite stock index rose 4.40 points to 704.16, off the daily high of 707.42.

"The ceiling expansion helped lift the market. Primary blue chips -- foreigners' favourite -- spearheaded the rises," said Kim Myung-ho of Hyundai Securities. The foreign stockholding limit will be raised to 23 percent from 20 percent on May 2.

"Investors anticipated at least 500 billion to 600 billion won would flow in, with the limit increase," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities. "Recently stabilising interest rates also bolstered investors' sentiment."
Among gaining blue chips, Samsung Electronics rose 500 won to 61,500 and SK Telecom added 1,000 won to 460,000.
POSCO also gained 1,100 won to 55,100. Brokers said hopes for a recovery in the steel industry contributed to the increase in steel shares. The iron and steel sub-index rose 19.24 points to 1,403.80.
Three Jinro affiliates went limit up on market talk that a committee of domestic financial institutions had decided to extend 100 billion won in emergency loans, brokers said.
Jinro Ltd, flagship of the Jinro Group, added 580 won to 7,890. Both Jinro Industries and Jinro General Foods rose 330 won and 320 won to 4,540 and 4,320 respectively.

But committee representatives denied the speculation and said the panel was still conferring. The voluntary committee was set up to prevent major corporate collapses following the earlier failures of Hanbo Steel Co and Sammi Steel Co.
"Investors believe the worst is over for the Jinro group," said Hwang of LG Securities.
The Securities Supervisory Board approved on Monday an application by Kookmin Bank to allow foreign investors to buy another 4.5 percent of its share capital.
Foreigners will be eligible to purchase an additional 4.18 million Kookmin shares on Friday.
Kookmin Bank briefly hit a 1997 high of 13,600 won but closed at 13,400, up 700 won.
Hwang of LG said the buying interest spread to banking shares, with its sub-index rising 2.70 percent to 364.91.
Brokers forecast a gradual rise on the index until the ceiling expansion but said there would be resistance around the 710 level.
